subject: Performance acceptance gates and validation roadmap (MAP) for Helios pilot
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus@helioshealth.com>, Ops Team <ops@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Performance acceptance gates and validation roadmap (MAP) for Helios pilot

Marcus / Helios ops team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I attached a draft MAP that folds the performance validation into the pilot close criteria so we can be explicit about what “go / no-go” looks like from a latency / throughput perspective. High level summary below and a few asks to lock the schedule: 

Workload slices (what we will test):
- Search/completion: mixed prompt mix (60% short prompts ~32 tokens, 40% long prompts ~512 tokens)
- Batch embedding calls for nightly indexing (single-call 256-dim vectors)
- Concurrency profile: steady-state lanes at 50, 200, 500 concurrent requests to represent web traffic vs peak-burst.

Primary SLOs / acceptance gates:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 120ms p95 on short prompts at 50 concurrency
- Generation latency (per-token) steady-state p95 <= 200ms for long prompts at 200 concurrency
- Throughput: sustained 1.2k tokens/sec across the pool during 500-concurrency stress window with <1% error rate
- Embedding wall-time: bulk 10k records completes within nightly window (2 hours) for batch job

Success criteria / exit:
- All SLOs met in a full run (3 cycles) OR agreed mitigation plan with quantized regressions and timeline for fixes
- No availability incidents causing >1 minute of total downtime during acceptance window

Schedule asks:
1) Confirm a 3-hour load window on Oct 6th (UTC 14:00–17:00) — Redwood runs staged ramp + two steady-state cycles.
2) Confirm test dataset and any sensitive fields we should mask (we will use synthetic data where requested).
3) Procurement: once MAP signed we will trigger the reserved pilot capacity request (invoice to procurement@helioshealth.com).

Attachments: helios_map_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), load-test-results-20260928.csv (baseline run from our lab), slo_summary.pdf (single-page SLO reference).

Can you review and confirm the schedule and dataset by EOD Friday? If fine, I’ll drop in Rishi and Evelyn to run pre-flight checks before the window.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Marcus Lee <marcus@helioshealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@helioshealth.com>, procurement@helioshealth.com
Date: 2026-09-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance gates and validation roadmap (MAP) for Helios pilot

Laura —

Thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. This looks promising. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock Oct 6: 

1) Concurrency targets: can you explain how you’ll simulate our mixed traffic (we have a mixture of interactive and queued jobs)? Will the 500 conc. run include the embedding batch or are those separate windows?

2) Measurement windows: for TTFT and per-token latency, are you measuring p95 over 1-minute rolling windows or over the full steady-state cycle? We need to align this with our SLAs.

3) Data handling: we will share a representative dataset but we require PII redaction and an inventory of any logs Redwood will store during the test (duration + retention).

Procurement: our team asked that the pilot PO reference the MAP doc and the deal id — I copied procurement. If you can send a short statement of work and estimated invoice timing we’ll queue internally.

We should be able to confirm the dataset and preliminary PO by Oct 4.

—Marcus
Marcus Lee
Director, Platform Engineering | Helios Health
marcus@helioshealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0123

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance gates and validation roadmap (MAP) for Helios pilot

Laura —

I’ll take the technical lead on this. Quick internal checklist based on Marcus’ questions: 

- Concurrency modeling: we'll run a hybrid driver where the 500-concurrency stress includes both interactive (65%) and queued/batch style requests (35%) so results reflect the mixed profile Marcus mentioned. We’ll separate an embedding-only run overnight to measure batch wall-time without interference.
- Measurement windows: agree to report p95 computed over the steady-state 10-minute windows; we’ll also include 1-minute rolling p95 diagnostics in the dashboard for visibility.
- Logs/retention: Evelyn — please prepare a brief evidence package: which logs we collect, retention period (default 30 days), and how PII is redacted during the run (synthetic masking + field-level redaction).

Evelyn, can you run a dry pre-flight on Oct 4 (30–60 minute run) and confirm the infra profile? I’ll set up the perf lab and load driver configs.

Laura — I’ll draft the short SOW snippet you can use for procurement referencing the MAP and the SLOs.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus@helioshealth.com>, Ops Team <ops@helioshealth.com>, procurement@helioshealth.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance acceptance gates and validation roadmap (MAP) for Helios pilot

Marcus — thank you, all. Summary / agreed next steps: 

- Concurrency: 500-concurrency stress will include mixed traffic (65% interactive, 35% queued). Separate embedding-only overnight run for batch wall-time.
- Measurement: p95 over steady-state 10-minute windows reported as primary; 1-minute rolling p95 provided as diagnostic.
- Data & logs: Redwood will only use sanitized/synthetic data for public runs; when Helios provides representative data we will apply field-level masking. Evidence package with retention policy (30 days) attached (slo_summary.pdf).
- Schedule: 
  - Oct 4 — dry pre-flight (Evelyn, Rishi) — 30–60 minutes.
  - Oct 6, 14:00–17:00 UTC — full MAP validation window (3 cycles).
  - Oct 8 — Redwood sends final results and a short remediation plan if any SLOs miss the targets.

Attachments included in this thread: helios_map_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), load-test-results-20260928.csv (baseline), slo_summary.pdf (evidence + retention).

Please reply with an ACK on the schedule and whether procurement needs any additional info from our SOW snippet (I’ll circulate once Rishi shares). If we get ACK by Oct 2 EOD, we’ll lock the slots and notify the lab.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Laura
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
